_readme: Everything on /recruiters comes from this file. Lists show in the order written, so put your best first: the home page shows the first 3 projects and first 5 achievements, and 'see all' pages show the rest. Leave a field as "" (or a list as []) to hide it. Format is documented in README.md.

profile.name: Pranav Umbarkar
profile.headline: B.Tech CSE (AI & DS) · NIT Warangal
profile.summary: Computer science student at NIT Warangal specialising in AI and data science. I like building systems end to end: LLM agents with LangGraph, routing engines over national road graphs, and data pipelines that turn messy web data into real signals. Winner of IEEEXtreme 2026 and 500+ problems solved on LeetCode.

points: Built an LLM-based PTO agent as a capstone project that processes employee leave requests and checks them against company leave policy.
Designed the agent's modular workflow and system architecture, separating request intake, policy evaluation, and decision logic for integration with enterprise systems.
Built a brand-protection data pipeline over 10,000+ ICANN domains, extracting features from SSL metadata, domain registration age, and scraped page content.
Developed a custom Logistic Regression and FuzzyWuzzy risk-scoring model on unstructured data, identifying 371 highly suspicious impersonating domains for threat analysis.

projects.name: Saarathi
projects.description: An India-wide routing platform for trucks carrying perishable crops. It picks routes by what spoilage would cost in rupees for that crop, not just by distance, and tells dispatchers when they must decide before a load goes bad.
points: Built an India-wide routing engine on a 591K-edge OpenStreetMap road graph (581,000 km), using corridor-pruned Dijkstra over crop-specific rupee costs to return routes in 0.4–2 s on most corridors.
Modelled spoilage from heat, humidity, vibration, and handling for 3 crops; cut projected wastage from 4.96% to 3.77% (24%) across 170 simulated shipments on real Agmarknet corridors.
Designed a human-in-the-loop dispatcher system that uses reverse Dijkstra to find each truck's point of no return and calculate decision deadlines.

projects.name: Autonomous AI Research Agent
projects.description: A two-agent system that reads arXiv papers, finds which ones are fair baselines to compare against, and checks research hypotheses against the full papers with a critic loop and a RAG validator.
points: Designed a dual-agent LangGraph pipeline that fetches arXiv papers, parses structured content with PyPDF, and runs parallel compatibility checks to filter valid comparative baselines.
Added a critic feedback loop for iterative refinement and a RAG-based validator (ChromaDB) that checks research hypotheses and answers questions against full paper corpora.
